newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-ACKERMANN BEGINS TWO-YEAR BAN AFTER LOSING APPEAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ACKERMANN BEGINS TWO-YEAR BAN AFTER LOSING APPEAL.

text.p: Former Springbok lock forward Johan Ackermann was beginning a two-year ban for doping on Thursday after the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) rejected his appeal against the punishment.

Ackermann and two Gauteng Lions players, Bennie Nortje and Stefan Bronkhorst, were originally banned in May after being found guilty of using the anabolic steroid nandrolene but all three appealed against the suspensions.
SARFU's appeals committee met at the weekend and decided to uphold the two-year bans.
Bronkhorst's brother Billy, a Northern Transvaal player, was also starting a two-year ban after admitting using an illegal substance.
A third Northerns player, prop forward Frikkie Bosman began a two-year suspension for a similar offence in April.

SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer said: "I am pleased that the sentences have stood. A strong message has been sent out to any player considering using illegal drugs that they will be caught and punished".
